decisions.reason: Full physical access to the ESP32-S3 pins does not change the established functional GPIO assignments.
The breakout decision does not alter the standalone USB power source, activation condition, capacity, or powered scope.
The reference to possible future projects with buttons describes the board's reuse rationale and does not change the current panel controls, connectors, mappings, or placement.
Retaining full through-hole pin access does not change the monitored rails, monitor IC, channel allocation, or measurement topology.
The generic-platform reuse rationale does not change the existing addressable-LED supply, switching, or logic-level requirements.
Full ESP32-S3 pin breakout access does not modify the I2C series-resistor value, population policy, purpose, or topology.

The source acknowledges routing constraints but does not change the board dimensions, orientation, connector placement, enclosure arrangement, or ESP32 edge placement. Breakout accommodation remains owned by the source Requirement.
The breakout change does not alter the OR-ing method, power sources, source-selection behavior, or diode requirement.
The source changes the separately modeled ESP32 breakout coverage, not the established JST and USB-C connector inventory or connector architecture.
Retaining a full through-hole breakout does not change the requirement for local decoupling capacitors.
The generic ESP32-S3 base-platform decision does not change the buzzer type or accepted component selection.
Full pin breakout access does not alter the switched 3.3V rail, switching side, MOSFET topology, or transistor pair.
